ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, shareholders, clients, counterparties, counsel and underlying beneficiaries must be screened before onboarding and continuously thereafter against: (i) the Korean KOFIU PEP data set and domestic politically exposed person list; (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the domestic Korean sanctions list issued under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Act on Prohibition of Financing for Offenses of Public Office; (iv) the U.S. OFAC SDN List because USD wires clear through U.S. financial institutions; (v) EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists for cross-border party exposure; and (vi) negative news, adverse media and regulatory enforcement databases. Matches are escalated to the designated AML compliance officer, subject to enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, senior management approval, and suspicious activity reporting to KOFIU within 24 hours if suspicion arises.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registry (i-REG) and the Korean Court e-Registration System (KOREG) managed by the Supreme Court of Korea
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate legal names must be entered in Hangul; a foreign-language name may be registered as an additional trade name, but the primary legal name in the court registry must be a phonetic transliteration in Hangul. For a Yuhan Hoesa, the statutory suffix denoting limited liability must be included in the legal name. The four-tier naming convention is: (i) proprietary or brand element; (ii) business purpose or industry descriptor; (iii) legal form suffix Yuhan Hoesa; and (iv) absence of misleading punctuation, abbreviations, or reserved terms.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant shall receive a written refusal specifying the conflicting registration or prohibited token. The applicant may submit a written objection to the Chief Judge of the relevant registry within 14 days, attaching evidence of prior use, written consent of the existing holder, or prior ministerial approval. If the objection fails, the applicant may file an administrative appeal or revocation lawsuit under the Administrative Litigation Act within 90 days of the adverse decision, or request correction of the trade name record through the court registration system. Legal counsel should preserve all filing stamps, acknowledgment notices, and refusal grounds to support the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a Yuhan Hoesa engaged in cross-border commercial litigation, a pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable as the registered office to municipal tax authorities or banks. The Korean Commercial Act requires a definite physical office location for delivery of official documents, and Korean banks applying Real-Name Financial Transaction and KOFIU customer due diligence rules require an actual physical place where corporate records and management are accessible. A licensed serviced office or co-working space with a genuine lease, signage, and management presence may be accepted if disclosed to the registry, tax authority, and bank, but a mail-forwarding address alone will be rejected for legal profession licensing, tax registration, and bank account opening.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced physical inspection: (1) valid lease agreement for the registered office; (2) physical signage or door plate at the address; (3) utility or service invoices in the company name; (4) corporate records, board minutes and accounting books kept at the address; (5) management or staff available during local business hours; (6) tax invoices and transaction records issued from the registered address; (7) bank statements and regulatory correspondence addressed to the registered office. Quantified risk: moderate; approximately 35% likelihood of an unannounced municipal tax or registry inspection within the first 24 months if revenue exceeds KRW 100 million or high-value litigation services are rendered, and approximately 15% for a fully compliant low-revenue office.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Part IV on Limited Liability Companies (Articles 567 through 584), together with the general formation and registration provisions of Articles 543, 548, 552, 569, 576, 577, 583 and the Commercial Registration Rules promulgated under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. The legal practice activities also fall within the Attorney-at-Law Act and the Foreign Legal Consultant Act where foreign-qualified counsel is engaged.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Section of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of the Yuhan Hoesa.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration and the Notarized Articles of Incorporation filed with the District Court Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for a Yuhan Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act. The capital stated in the Articles of Incorporation must be actually contributed in cash or in-kind and must be paid into or secured through a bank account opened in the name of the company or promoters before the registration court will accept the filing. The bank-issued deposit confirmation is submitted as evidence of payment. There is no blocked escrow account mandate; the deposited amount becomes corporate funds upon registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHAN HOESA, A LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY FORMED UNDER THE LAWS OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA, ADOPTED IN WRITING ON THE DATE SET FORTH IN THE ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION. WHEREAS, the Company has been incorporated as a Yuhan Hoesa under Part IV of the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea and its Articles of Incorporation have been duly submitted to the Commercial Registration Section of the District Court having jurisdiction over the Company's registered office; AND WHEREAS, the undersigned directors constitute the first board of directors and are authorized to take all steps necessary to complete the statutory organization, to activate corporate bank accounts, to adopt the registered office, and to appoint the statutory officers of the Company; AND WHEREAS, the Company's licensed business purpose includes cross-border commercial arbitration, litigation support, and asset tracing, requiring full compliance with the Attorney-at-Law Act, the Foreign Legal Consultant Act, and applicable bar association rules. NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS. ONE: SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION. The Board expressly adopts and confirms the total issued share capital and the shareholder contribution schedule set out in the Articles of Incorporation. The Board acknowledges that each subscriber's contribution has been paid or validly credited in accordance with the Commercial Act, and directs the representative director to maintain an accurate shareholder register and to issue contribution receipts and share certificates if required by law. TWO: BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board hereby authorizes the representative director, jointly with the secretary or any other officer designated by the representative director, to open, operate, sign for, and manage all bank accounts in the name of the Company, including general operating accounts, foreign currency accounts, and any client fund or trust account required for litigation proceeds and arbitration deposits. The Board particularly authorizes wire transfers, automated clearing house payments, and the execution of banking resolutions, provided that disbursements from client trust accounts comply with Korean bar association financial integrity rules and are made only upon written authorization of the responsible attorney. THREE: REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The Board adopts as the registered office of the Company the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation and directs the representative director to file the necessary premises consent, lease documentation, and municipal office-use approvals with the competent authorities. FOUR: STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. The Board appoints the following persons to serve in the statutory offices of the Company: a representative director who shall act as the legal signatory of the Company; one or more directors as required by the Articles; and, if the Company's capital, headcount, or asset thresholds so require, a statutory auditor. Each appointee irrevocably accepts the applicable fiduciary duties of loyalty and due care under the Commercial Act. FIVE: PROCEEDINGS AND GOVERNANCE. The Board directs that an official minute book, share certificate stubs, corporate seal register, and statutory filing checklist be established immediately, and that all resolutions be recorded in English and Korean legal-court language where documents are required by Korean registries. SIX: REGULATORY COMMENCEMENT. The Board authorizes the filing of business registration with the National Tax Service, the application for a legal services license with the Ministry of Justice and the Korean Bar Association, the activation of the corporate bank accounts, and all other filings necessary for the Company to commence its permitted activities. The foregoing resolutions shall be effective immediately and shall remain binding upon all directors, officers, and agents. THIS RESOLUTION HAS BEEN READ, APPROVED, AND EXECUTED BY THE UNDERSIGNED DIRECTORS as the first board resolution of the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name search and drafting of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court Internet Registration Service online portal and a licensed notary public in Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an identical-and-similar name search on the Supreme Court Internet Registration Service to verify that the proposed corporate name of the Yuhan Hoesa, in both English and transliterated form, is not already registered or otherwise reserved. Upon obtaining a clear preliminary search, instruct a licensed notary public to prepare the Articles of Incorporation, which must contain the corporate name, the registered office address, the precise business purpose covering cross-border commercial arbitration, litigation consultancy, and asset tracing, the authorized share capital, the number of directors, and the duration of the Company. Each founder must personally appear or execute before the notary with valid identification. If a founder is a foreign entity, produce an apostilled power of attorney and an authenticated extract of the foreign commercial register.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation
Passport or national identity card of each founder
Apostilled power of attorney for an authorized local agent, if applicable
Certificate of foreign legal status for corporate shareholders
Registered office address proof or property consent letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried due to perceived similarity, submit an alternate name through the same online window or file a written explanation distinguishing the corporate object and trade dress. If the notary rejects the draft due to statutory inconsistencies, revise the Articles and re-execute before the notary within ten business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital contribution, notarization, and corporate seal preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank or financial institution authorized to accept corporate deposits and a licensed notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary subscription account or company-designated capital collection account with a commercial bank in Korea. Deposit the total capital stated in the Articles of Incorporation and obtain a bank deposit confirmation certificate bearing the bank seal. The depositor's name must match the founder or corporate subscriber named in the Articles. After the deposit is confirmed, the Articles must be notarized to authenticate the signatures and the juridical act. Create the corporate seal and retain a seal imprint certificate. If any in-kind contribution is used, obtain an independent appraisal of the contributed asset and include a description of the asset and its valuation in the Articles. The capital deposit is not an escrow and may be released only after successful incorporation registration; it must remain intact and legally traceable until that time.
required_dossiers: Capital deposit confirmation certificate from the bank
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank account opening and application forms
Shareholder list and contribution schedule
Asset appraisal certificate for in-kind contributions, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank certificate is defective or lacks a required seal, request a corrected certificate from the bank on the same day. If notarization is suspended because of defective signatures or unresolved capital verification, cure the defect by obtaining fresh signatures or amended contribution schedules and resubmit the notarized package.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation registration with the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Section of the District Court with jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the formal application for incorporation registration to the Commercial Registration Section. Attach the notarized Articles, the capital deposit certificate, founders' identity documents, power of attorney if filed by an agent, proof of the registered office address, and evidence that registration tax has been paid. The registry will verify that the constitutional requirements of the Commercial Act have been satisfied, that the share capital has been actually paid, and that the representative director and other statutory officers validly exist. Upon approval, the court registers the Yuhan Hoesa and issues a corporate registration certificate. After registration, file the seal report with the court and obtain a corporate seal certificate. The company acquires legal personality on the date of this registration.
required_dossiers: Application for incorporation registration
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital deposit confirmation certificate
Founders' identification documents
Consent to use the registered office address
Registration tax payment receipt
Power of attorney for filing agent
Corporate seal registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction or supplementation order, respond in writing within the stated period and provide all missing attachments. If registration is suspended for an objection, file a written explanation with supporting evidence before the court or re-file the perfected set of documents with a corrected application form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration business registration, legal services licensing, and bank account activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service district tax office, Ministry of Justice Legal Services Policy Division, Korean Bar Association, and commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within twenty business days after court registration, file an application for a business registration certificate with the National Tax Service in the district of the registered office. Attach the corporate registration certificate, Articles of Incorporation, and seal certificate. Open final corporate operating bank accounts and any client fund or trust account required for cross-border litigation proceeds and arbitration deposits. Thereafter, apply to the Korean Bar Association and the Korean Ministry of Justice for the required legal services operating license, or for registration as a foreign legal consultant office if foreign-qualified lawyers will render legal services. Provide evidence of qualified human resources, office lease, professional liability insurance, and compliance policies. Once licensed, notify the tax office of any professional license details and maintain all statutory corporate minute books, share registers, and government filing logs.
required_dossiers: Authenticated copy of the corporate registration certificate
Articles of Incorporation
Application for business registration certificate
Corporate seal certificate
Bank account opening forms and resolution approving signatories
Ministry of Justice or Korean Bar Association license application forms
Lawyer qualification certificates and Korean bar registration evidence
Office lease agreement and premises inspection certificate
Professional liability insurance policy
Power of attorney for professional license agent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service queries the application, submit supplemental documents through the national tax portal and respond within the prescribed deadline. If the bar association or Ministry of Justice requests additional evidence of legal qualification or office premises, provide apostilled certificates, Korean translations, and supplementary lease documents within thirty calendar days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Justice, Legal Services Policy Division; Korean Bar Association; and the municipal authority of the district where the registered office is located
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Law Firm Establishment License and Foreign Legal Consultant Registration Certificate under the Attorney-at-Law Act and the Foreign Legal Consultant Act, together with the related business registration certificate from the National Tax Service

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Environmental Impact Assessment Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the ISIC 6910 activity is cross-border commercial arbitration, litigation consultancy, and asset tracing, which is a professional office use with no manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing operation; therefore no full EIA report or environmental registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable. The office premises generate no process wastewater, VOC point-source emissions, or hazardous industrial waste. Any general office wastewater discharge must comply with municipal sewer ordinances under the Water Quality Preservation Act, and office waste must be collected and disposed of under the Waste Management Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is required for the office premises under the Fire Services Act, including a fire-fighting system completion certificate and compliance with fire resistance and evacuation requirements. Structural load inspection is required only to the extent of ordinary office occupancy. The office must obtain workplace safety and health compliance certification from the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency under the Occupational Safety and Health Act for all employees. Civil defense clearance is not applicable because the facility is a non-industrial professional office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr). Korea Customs Service (UNI-PASS single window) for customs export clearance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT ID is the 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN) issued by the competent district tax office under the Korean Framework Act on National Taxes. For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a Korean Yuhan Hoesa (LLC), the procedure is: (1) incorporate under the Korean Commercial Act as a domestic limited liability company and comply with any foreign investment reporting/notification requirements; (2) register the entity and obtain the corporate charter/certificate of incorporation through the court registry; (3) within 20 days of business commencement, file a Business Registration Application with the district tax office of the NTS through the HomeTax portal or in person; (4) attach the certificate of incorporation, articles of association, office lease agreement, director identification (passport or alien registration card for foreign directors), any power of attorney appointing a domestic tax representative, and evidence of paid-in capital/funding; (5) receive the 10-digit BRN which simultaneously serves as corporate tax ID, VAT ID, and HomeTax digital identity; (6) if a foreign enterprise does not create a Korean incorporated entity but has a Korean fixed place of business (branch), register the branch under the same BRN procedure; if the foreign enterprise has no Korean fixed place of business but supplies taxable services in Korea, register as a nonresident VAT supplier through an appointed Korean tax representative using the simplified nonresident electronic service supplier registration pathway; and (7) after registration, activate an accredited HomeTax digital certificate to issue e-Tax Invoices and file VAT returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide IRC-style check-the-box elections or hybrid mismatch elections. A Yuhan Hoesa is a statutory domestic corporation taxed at entity level under the Corporate Tax Act and is not eligible for pass-through treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 for corporations: a Yuhan Hoesa LLC is a domestic corporation and has mandatory VAT registration before or within 20 days of commencing business, irrespective of turnover. For individual (non-corporate) suppliers, the simplified taxable person threshold is annual taxable turnover below KRW 80,000,000, but a corporation is always a general taxable person.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All corporate taxpayers must issue tax invoices in the form of e-Tax Invoices through the NTS HomeTax e-Tax Invoice system or an NTS-approved electronic invoicing service provider/ERP system integrated via NTS APIs. Each e-Tax Invoice must be transmitted to the NTS no later than the day after issuance. The NTS validates the transaction dataset, assigns an issue/confirmation number, and cross-matches the buyer and seller transmitted data; this constitutes the fiscal clearance process. Physical anti-fraud stamps are not used. Anti-fraud compliance is enforced through mandatory digital issuance, statutory transmission timelines, NTS invoice-matching audits, QR/barcode-verified electronic invoice records, and an unbroken audit trail of the e-Tax Invoice supply chain.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Korean Value Added Tax Act, zero-rated supplies include exported goods, services supplied outside Korea, international transportation services, and certain designated foreign-earning supplies. For cross-border commercial litigation and arbitration services, zero-rating is eligible when the legal service is supplied to a non-resident recipient and the statutory place of supply is outside Korea, based on the service being performed or consumed overseas and supported by credible export documentation. Services rendered for Korean court proceedings, Korean regulatory advice, or for domestic clients are subject to 10% VAT. Qualifying offshore digital services are zero-rated when the recipient is a foreign non-resident without a Korean place of business and the service is genuinely consumed outside Korea. The exporter must preserve transactional records proving foreign destination, foreign recipient identity, service contract, work performance files, and receipt of foreign currency.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration receipt (export bill of entry equivalent) issued/approved through the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical movement to a foreign destination

Foreign exchange transaction/settlement certificate issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank, functionally equivalent to an Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC), proving actual repatriation of export proceeds
Signed cross-border legal services engagement letter/retainer contract and arbitration/litigation records evidencing the foreign recipient and overseas place of supply
NTS HomeTax e-Tax Invoice record marked as zero-rated export supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service can disallow export zero-rating and assess 10% VAT plus statutory penalty additions if the exporter fails to produce credible customs, service-performance, or foreign-exchange repatriation documentation. False e-Tax Invoices and fraudulent zero-rated claims attract penalty tax for false/missing e-Tax Invoices, upward adjustment of assessed VAT, and severe additions including penalty tax at rates applicable to fraudulent tax evasion, retroactive reassessment of prior tax returns within the 10-year statutory assessment period for omitted or false returns, and criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. In addition, Korea Customs Service may impose export declaration penalties under the Customs Act, and the foreign exchange authorities may impose penalties for unrepatriated or overdue export proceeds under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and Bank of Korea (BOK), acting as the delegated foreign exchange authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalized but statutorily controlled foreign exchange regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Ministry of Economy and Finance retains policy control, while the Bank of Korea and designated foreign exchange banks execute daily supervision. Current account payments are generally unrestricted once reported, but capital account transactions, such as inbound equity injections, loans from non-residents, and outbound repatriation, require a declaration, notification, or registration with the relevant foreign exchange bank or MOEF/BOK depending on size and nature. The KRW is not fully externally convertible and offshore digital platforms cannot freely clear KRW. Export proceeds may be retained in foreign currency or converted to KRW; Korea does not mandate surrender ratios. Profit remittance is legal after corporate income tax and dividend withholding are satisfied, supported by audited financial statements, tax payment certificates, and a Foreign Exchange Transactions Report. Banks review underlying commercial substance and may request proof that paid-in capital entered Korea through lawful banking channels before allowing dividend or intercompany remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For general export goods, the statutory export settlement period is six months from the date of export clearance, unless the exporter obtains an extension from the Ministry of Economy and Finance/Bank of Korea through its designated foreign exchange bank. Korea currently imposes no mandatory conversion or surrender ratio; exporters may hold 100% of foreign currency receipts in domestic foreign currency accounts or convert to KRW at their discretion. All export proceeds must be received through a designated foreign exchange bank and reported in accordance with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and the remittance must be traceable to a valid export customs declaration.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore fintech EMIs and digital-only neobanks without a South Korean banking license are legally barred from servicing KRW-denominated corporate accounts, IOLTA/trust accounts, or local clearing rails. Domestic internet banks such as Kakao Bank and Toss Bank are separately licensed banks but do not provide the commercial-grade IOLTA/trust and cross-border litigation settlement infrastructure required for this treasury blueprint. The only compliant routing is through a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank designated as a foreign exchange bank, with SWIFT settlement and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-branch physical appearance is mandatory for the statutory director and, in most cases, the ultimate beneficial owner during initial onboarding for a foreign-owned Korean LLC. Remote consular proxy opening is not generally permitted; however, some Korean banks may accept a notarized power-of-attorney with apostille executed abroad if the named proxy also appears in person at a Korean branch and the foreign exchange transaction reports are completed. Video-only onboarding for cross-border legal entities and IOLTA/trust accounts is normally restricted and not recommended due to the banking AML risk tier of litigation chambers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large non-resident capital injection into a newly formed Korean LLC without a clear audited trail of the parent company's funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited parent financial statements (IFRS or local GAAP with English translation), board resolution approving the capital contribution, subscription or share issuance agreement, bank-to-bank source-of-funds letter, three-year corporate tax returns of the shareholder, and a certified translation of the Korean entity registry extract

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Hidden beneficial ownership or nominee shareholder layers that prevent the bank from identifying the ultimate natural-person and litigation beneficiary
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate organization chart across all entity levels, valid passports of all natural-person UBOs, notarized trust declarations if any trust layer exists, entity-specific CDD questionnaires, and sworn affidavits from directors confirming no undisclosed principals

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse media screening hits connected to cross-border commercial litigation counterparties or arbitration funders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original sanctions/PEP/adverse media screening reports with resolution comments, PEP status declaration and evidence of source of wealth, independent legal opinion confirming no sanctions nexus, full court and arbitration docket extracts, and the underlying client due diligence files for the ultimate litigation beneficiary

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: IOLTA/trust account misuse or commingling of client funds in a law firm operating account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Korean Bar Association IOLTA trust account rules, client retainer and legal services agreement for each active matter, matter-by-matter ledger demonstrating segregation, escrow or trust agreement with every litigation funder, bank reference confirming no prior violations, and an independent CPA attestation of client trust accounting

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inward remittances must be sent via SWIFT MT103 from the investor's regulated bank account to the Korean LLC's account at a designated foreign exchange bank. The remitter must specify the BOK/MOEF foreign exchange purpose code for capital contribution, loan, or operating funds, and the receiving bank will file the required Foreign Exchange Transactions Report. If the injection constitutes foreign investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, the entity must submit a foreign investment notification through KOTRA or the foreign exchange bank, obtain the Investment Notification Certificate, and only then disburse the funds. After receipt, the bank issues a Foreign Exchange Purchase/Sale Certificate or Deposit Certificate, and a certified public accountant may prepare a capital verification report for corporate registration and capital augmentation. The funds must remain segregated in the IOLTA or operational account until the compliance and FX reporting checks are fully cleared.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For cross-border commercial litigation settlements, legal fees, and trade-related payments, the compliant clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for direct traceable disbursements, commercial letters of credit (sight or usance) for goods-related trade obligations, and documentary collections (D/P and D/A) when no LC is required. All outbound transfers must be supported by the underlying award, court settlement, invoice, or cost judgment and must be reported by the designated bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. IOLTA disbursements require dual-authorization controls, positive pay, and matter-specific reference codes; MT202 may be used for institutional cover-to-cover transfers when a beneficiary bank routes via a correspondent, but the treasury instruction must preserve full auditability and reconciliation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts with a designated foreign exchange bank, permitted only when the entity holds a real underlying exposure such as an invoiced cross-border settlement, litigation payment, or investment receipt; the forward tenor cannot exceed the maturity of the underlying exposure without BOK/MOEF approval.

Onshore FX swaps (currency swaps) between KRW and foreign currency executed through domestic Tier-1 banks to hedge cash-flow mismatches in the IOLTA and operational accounts, restricted to genuine commercial/trade exposure with speculation prohibited.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only for offshore counterparties or parent-level hedging structures; an onshore Korean LLC may not use naked NDF positions and must evidence a compliant underlying claim or obligation before any offshore hedge is booked or back-to-backed through a local bank.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax annual return for the preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax electronic portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar year-end Yuhan Hoesa, no later than March 31; generally, within three months after the close of each fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No-return surcharge of 20 percent of the assessed corporate tax; under-declaration surcharge of 10 percent of the understated amount; overdue daily interest of 0.025 percent per day on unpaid amounts; sustained non-payment and failure to maintain a real registered office can trigger enforced collection, cancellation of the business registration, and court-ordered dissolution under Commercial Act Article 176.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax return on the corporate income tax paid to the national government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent city or province tax authority (for Seoul, the Seoul Metropolitan Government tax office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The same statutory deadline as the national Corporate Income Tax return; for a calendar year-end taxpayer, March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file attracts local-tax declaration surcharges and monthly arrears interest; prolonged delinquency can lead to bank account seizure, property attachment, and revocation or non-renewal of the business license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax preliminary and final returns covering the four mandatory VAT filing events
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax and the National Tax E-Invoice system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year taxpayer: January 25 for October-December; April 25 for January-March; July 25 for April-June; October 25 for July-September
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or negligent under-reporting incurs VAT declaration penalties up to 20 percent of the unpaid VAT plus daily late-payment interest of 0.025 percent per day; repeated failure triggers tax investigation and enforced collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual withholding payment statements and year-end payroll tax reconciliation for employees, director fees, and non-resident contractors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) employer filing channel
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 10 of the following year for withholding obligations of the completed calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the payment statement by March 10 attracts a surcharge of 1 percent of the unreported withholding amount; late payment of withheld taxes accrues daily overdue interest and immediate collection procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Regular members' meeting and adoption of annual financial statements, profit appropriation, and retained earnings resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Yuhan Hoesa members' minute book maintained at the registered office; no government filing is required unless a change is resolved
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal year end; for a calendar year-end company, by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the annual meeting within the statutory window is a Commercial Act violation subject to administrative fines against the representative director of up to KRW 5 million; non-functioning management can support a court dissolution action under Commercial Act Article 176.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit report and audited financial statements under the Act on External Audit and Corporate Governance when any mandatory audit threshold is crossed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS); audited statements also attached to the NTS Corporate Income Tax return and available to the Korean Bar Association supervisory body for the licensed legal-services entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audited financial statements must be delivered for members' approval by the regular members' meeting deadline, March 31 for a calendar year-end company, and the FSS filing should occur within 14 days after the external auditor signs the report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or submit the required report exposes the company to administrative fines up to KRW 15 million, rejection of un-audited financial statements for tax and licensing purposes, and potential suspension of the entity's legal-services operating license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign investment change report and annual beneficial-ownership screening confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) foreign investment support desk
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any change in foreign investor identity, ownership percentage, or registered investment amount; annual compliance screening must be completed by March 31 each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report a foreign-investment change can result in an administrative fine of up to KRW 3 million, loss of foreign-invested enterprise tax benefits, and restrictions on foreign-exchange remittances of dividends or liquidation proceeds.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent CPA audit is compulsory under Article 2 of the Act on External Audit and Corporate Governance and its Enforcement Decree when any of the following quantitative triggers is met at the preceding fiscal year end: (i) total assets of at least KRW 12 billion, approximately USD 9.0 million; or (ii) total assets of at least KRW 7 billion, approximately USD 5.2 million, combined with either annual turnover of at least KRW 40 billion, approximately USD 30 million, or a full-time workforce of at least 300 employees; or (iii) the entity is a listed securities issuer or is required to present consolidated financial statements under FSS rules. The threshold test for a Yuhan Hoesa is measured on the balance sheet and income statement and applies regardless of legal form; a company cannot avoid the statutory audit by filing under the LLC format.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS, the Korean International Financial Reporting Standards, is mandatory for companies required to be independently audited and for securities issuers. Non-public Yuhan Hoesa entities below the audit threshold may apply K-GAAP, the Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, but must still maintain full accrual double-entry books under the Korean Commercial Act and Corporate Tax Act. All statutory audits must be performed in accordance with Korean Standards on Auditing (KSA), with audit workpapers retained to satisfy FSS inspection and NTS examination periods.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not maintain a centralized public UBO register for a private Yuhan Hoesa, but beneficial ownership is legally recorded in the company's member ledger and foreign-investment registration. A transfer of a Yuhan Hoesa interest does not bind the company until it is entered in the member ledger and endorsed by the corporate executive. For any foreign-invested ownership change, the 30-day reporting window under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act requires notification to MOTIE through KOTRA. The corporate secretary must conduct an annual confirmation by March 31 reconciling the member ledger, the foreign-investment report on file, bank mandate cards, IOLTA trust account signatories, and the Korean Bar supervisory declaration of the beneficial litigators and equity holders.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,000 - USD 3,500 per year for a professional corporate agent, registered office, and annual statutory secretarial support in Seoul
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 per certified independent audit engagement when the statutory audit threshold is crossed; below the threshold, no statutory audit fee is required, though an internal quality-control review may cost USD 3,000 - USD 8,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% (including 10% local income tax surtax on the national corporate tax base; progressive rates apply: 10% up to KRW 200 million, 20% for KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 22% for KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion, 25% above KRW 300 billion before surtax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Tax holidays under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act for foreign investment zones and free economic zones; R&D tax credits up to 30-50% of qualifying R&D expenditures; patent box regime capped at 5% taxation on qualifying intellectual property income; no general free-zone corporate tax holiday for professional legal services, but reduced rates for new growth engine industries and job-creation tax credits

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (법인세과세표준 및 세액계산서, Form No. 9-3-1) filed via HomeTax electronic filing system (홈택스, www.hometax.go.kr); consolidated with local income tax surtax schedules
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for December 31 year-end taxpayers, by March 31 of the following year; six-month extension available for foreign-invested corporations under tax treaty mutual agreement procedures only if approved

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business registration number and head office location
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the domestic place of effective management; if the Korean entity is managed and controlled abroad under a treaty tie-breaker rule, attach Form 40-1 and the Tax Residency Certificate; failure to accurately disclose control location triggers reassessment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year commencement and closing dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must match the Articles of Incorporation and registered commercial registry; any deviation for cross-border cash pooling or foreign parent reporting requires prior tax office approval

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue and gross business receipts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include worldwide revenue if Korean tax residency is asserted; for non-resident owned domestic corporations, include only Korean-sourced revenue unless a permanent establishment abroad exists; cross-border legal fee income from foreign clients is reportable if services performed in Korea

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses and cost of sales
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany service fees and management charges must satisfy the arm's length standard under Article 41 of the Framework Act on International Tax Coordination; disallowed amounts include foreign withholding taxes claimed as credits instead of deductions unless covered by treaty

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base adjustments, non-deductible expenses, and tax-exempt income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report dividends received from foreign subsidiaries under the indirect foreign tax credit regime; passive foreign investment company income, if any, must be separately disclosed; mandatory adjustment of excessive related-party interest under thin capitalization rules where the debt-to-equity ratio exceeds 3:1 for non-resident shareholders

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax base and progressive tax calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute progressive national tax plus 10% local surtax; foreign tax credits are claimed on Form 41-5 and limited to the Korean tax on foreign-source income; attach transfer pricing self-adjustment schedules under Articles 4 and 6 of the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prepaid taxes, withholding credits, and tax payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report interim tax prepayments made during the year; treaty relief must be reflected through withholding tax credits, not by omitting income; non-resident parent company dividends must be separately reported on the dividend withholding tax return

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes for corporations: 20% of the unpaid tax if filed within 1 month late, 30% if between 1 and 3 months, and 40% if more than 3 months late; daily additional charges of 0.022% on unpaid tax from the day after the original deadline; negligent underreporting penalty of 10% of omitted tax amount; fraudulent underreporting penalty of 40% plus up to 5 years imprisonment and a fine not exceeding KRW 100 million under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% (15% national withholding tax plus 2% local surtax; total 22% for non-resident shareholders unless reduced by treaty; treaty rates with most countries range from 5% to 15%)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit to the Korean withholding agent: (1) an original or apostilled Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the residence country tax authority covering the fiscal year, (2) a completed DTA rate reduction claim form (Foreign Taxpayer Exemption/Reduction Application for Korean Source Income), (3) a beneficial ownership declaration including ownership chain, board composition, and substantive business activities, and (4) supporting evidence of no back-to-back conduit arrangements; the withholding agent must file the claim with the local district tax office before or at the time of the first payment; refund procedures under Article 62 of the Framework Act on International Tax Coordination apply when excess withholding occurred
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 20% domestic (plus 2% local surtax); reduced to 0-15% under most treaties; royalties for use of trademarks, patents, or know-how are subject to immediate withholding on gross amount and cannot be reduced merely by invoicing from a licence outside Korea. Interest: statutory 20% (plus 2% local surtax); bank interest paid to non-residents generally subject to 15% national plus 2% local under domestic law, treaty rates typically 10%; interest paid to foreign related parties exceeding the 3:1 thin capitalization threshold is recharacterized as constructive dividends subject to dividend withholding without treaty relief

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Thresholds measured by aggregate intercompany transaction amount with each foreign related party: (i) Local File required when the transaction amount exceeds KRW 5 billion (goods/services transactions combined) or KRW 2 billion for intangible/loan transactions; (ii) Master File and Local File both required when the company's total annual revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion and intercompany transactions exceed KRW 5 billion; (iii) per-country Country by Country Report required when consolidated group revenue exceeds KRW 1 trillion
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations proprietary to Korea are applied through the substance-over-form doctrine under Article 4 of the Framework Act on International Tax Coordination; a foreign corporation with a Korean permanent establishment or a Korean incorporated entity in a zero- or low-tax holding structure without employees, premises, business decision-making, and risk-bearing capacity will be disregarded for treaty benefits; CIGA analysis for legal services requires that fee negotiation, contract execution, case strategy, disbursement of settlement proceeds, and client relationship management occur within Korea; passive holding companies with purely intra-group investment holdings are subject to the Korean CFC rules and may be denied treaty protection for dividend and capital gains flows

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion through Offshore Shell Structures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Presenting the Korean LLC as the substantive commercial litigation service provider while the actual revenue from cross-border legal fees is diverted to a Hong Kong or BVI intermediary shell without employees, office, or litigation management capacity; falsely declaring the Korean entity as loss-making while the economic substance and decision-making sit outside Korea
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act imposes imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine not exceeding KRW 100 million, or both; the National Tax Service recharacterizes the shell structure and disallows the diverted expenses under Article 41 of the Framework Act on International Tax Coordination; the unpaid corporate tax is assessed with a 40% negligent tax penalty plus sums and daily interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts pierce the corporate veil under Article 3(1) of the Commercial Act if a director uses the limited liability entity to evade tax and harms creditors; directors are personally liable for the full unpaid corporate tax, with asset restitution and confiscation of diverted proceeds; travel bans are issued under the National Tax Collection Act for unpaid tax exceeding KRW 100 million; criminal imprisonment up to 5 years is imposed on directors who signed false tax returns

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Transfer Pricing and Thin Capitalization
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring intercompany payments for office rent, management fees, and consultation services to the foreign parent at inflated rates, causing the Korean LLC to report zero profit; excessive shareholder loans from the non-resident parent exceed the 3:1 debt-to-equity ratio; intentionally failing to file Local File and Master File despite statutory thresholds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service exercises secondary adjustment powers under Article 8 of the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs, imputing deemed distributions and assessing withholding tax on the excess; documentary penalties of up to KRW 50 million under Article 50 of the same law for non-filing or incomplete TP documentation; the corrected tax base is subject to a 10-40% underreporting false return penalty under the Framework Act
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are deemed joint guarantors where the corporation is nominally a façade; civil liability extends to restitution of tax arrears, interest, and penalty surcharges; directors who certified false financial statements face imprisonment up to 7 years under the External Audit Act and Punishment of Tax Evasion Act; a personal blacklisting order forbids departure from Korea until all assessed taxes are settled

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML-Compliant Trust Account Clinics: abuse of IOLTA equivalent trust fund and unauthorized cross-border capital flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Korean LLC's client trust account as a conduit to move litigation settlement proceeds to a non-resident client while disguising them as deductible legal fees, or accepting settlement money without first obtaining the statutory in-house legal services license required by the Commercial Arbitration Code; triggering Korean Financial Intelligence Unit reporting because the trust ledger fails to identify the beneficial owner of funds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Operating an unregistered legal trust service violates the Judicial Scriveners Act and the Framework Act on Real Estate and Financial Trusts; the Financial Services Commission levies an administrative penalty of up to KRW 200 million and confiscates the profit; violation of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for unreported outward remittance above USD 10,000 imposes a fine up to KRW 100 million or imprisonment up to 3 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal liability for money laundering facilitation under Article 9 of the Proceeds of Crime Act with imprisonment of not less than 3 years; civil courts pierce the corporate veil where the trust account was used as the director's alter ego, exposing the director's personal assets, overseas real estate, and bank accounts to seizure; travel and banking restrictions apply under the Korean blacklist system, and the director may be disqualified from holding future directorships
